He was married to Seema Sajdeh
Seema documented post-divorce life on Netflix's Fabulous Lives of Bollywood Wives

stories.headline: Imtiaz Ali Fires Back at Trolls: 'Indian Muslims Proved Their Patriotism by Choosing to Stay'
stories.what: Filmmaker Imtiaz Ali has hit back at online trolls questioning the patriotism of Indian Muslims, stating that their very decision to remain in India after Partition is itself proof of their loyalty to the country. His remarks came amid a charged social-media atmosphere and have sparked widespread debate. Ali, known for films such as Rockstar and Tamasha, is one of the more prominent voices from Bollywood to speak out on the issue in recent weeks. The statement has drawn both support and criticism across platforms.
stories.lens: When a filmmaker of Imtiaz Ali's standing publicly pushes back against communal trolling, it reflects the growing pressure on public figures to either speak or stay silent on questions of identity and belonging in India.
stories.article:
Filmmaker Imtiaz Ali has pushed back sharply against trolls who have questioned the patriotism of Indian Muslims, arguing that the community's decision to stay in India — rather than migrate to Pakistan at Partition — is itself an unambiguous demonstration of their loyalty to the country. "Indian Muslims have proved their patriotism by deciding to stay in India," Ali said, in remarks that quickly spread across social media.

The statement arrives at a moment of heightened communal sensitivity, with online discourse frequently targeting Muslim public figures and ordinary citizens alike with demands that they prove their national allegiance. Ali's intervention, blunt and without diplomatic hedging, was seen as a direct rebuke of that culture of suspicion.

Reaction was swift and polarised. Supporters praised Ali for speaking plainly on a subject many in the film industry prefer to avoid, while critics accused him of politicising the conversation or mischaracterising the history of Partition. The debate around the remarks quickly overshadowed discussion of his recent or upcoming film work.

Ali joins a small but growing number of Bollywood figures who have chosen to engage publicly with questions of Muslim identity in India rather than deflect them. Whether his intervention shifts the tone of online discourse or merely intensifies it remains to be seen, but the fact that such a statement now constitutes headline news underlines just how contested these questions of citizenship and belonging have become in contemporary India.
key_facts: Imtiaz Ali said Indian Muslims proved patriotism by staying in India post-Partition
Remarks were a direct response to online trolls
Ali is known for directing films such as Rockstar and Tamasha

stories.headline: Anjali Anand on Bell Bottom: 'I Was Only There So a Terrorist Could Fall on Top of Me'
stories.what: Actor Anjali Anand has spoken with sharp self-deprecating humour about her experience filming Bell Bottom, the 2021 Akshay Kumar-led thriller, saying her role amounted to being present so a terrorist could fall on top of her. The candid remark sheds light on the frustrations many supporting actors in Bollywood face — hired for fleeting, underdeveloped roles regardless of their ability. Anand, who has since built a stronger profile in streaming projects, used the comment to reflect on how far she has come since those early days in the industry.
stories.lens: Anjali Anand's wry observation about being cast as little more than a prop in a big-budget film puts a human face on the systemic underuse of talent that Bollywood's star-driven model routinely produces.
stories.article:
Actor Anjali Anand has delivered one of the more memorable lines of candour about Bollywood's treatment of supporting talent, saying of her appearance in the 2021 action-thriller Bell Bottom: "I was in Bell Bottom only so a terrorist could fall on top of me." The remark, delivered with evident wit, cuts to the heart of an experience many peripheral cast members know well but rarely articulate publicly.

Bell Bottom, starring Akshay Kumar and based loosely on 1980s hijacking episodes, was a high-profile production — one of the first major Bollywood films to release in cinemas during the Covid-19 pandemic. For a supporting actor, securing a role in such a project carries obvious appeal. The reality of what that role entails, however, can be rather less glamorous, as Anand's comment makes plain.

Since her early Bollywood appearances, Anand has found a more substantial platform in streaming content, where ensemble casts and character-driven narratives tend to give supporting actors greater room to demonstrate range. The contrast between her Bell Bottom experience and her more recent work seems to have given her both the perspective and the confidence to speak about it with humour.

Her comments have resonated strongly online, where many actors — particularly women — have spoken about being cast in roles that exist primarily to serve the male lead's storyline. Anand's specific, funny formulation of the problem has given that broader conversation a vivid new shorthand.
key_facts: Anjali Anand said her Bell Bottom role was only to have a terrorist fall on her
Bell Bottom (2021) starred Akshay Kumar
Anand has since built her profile through streaming projects

stories.headline: Jasmine Sandlas Announces Engagement Live on Stage at Delhi Concert
stories.what: Singer Jasmine Sandlas, known for the hit song Dhurandhar, publicly introduced her fiancé to the audience during a live concert in Delhi, saying "This is my man" from the stage. The moment, unscripted and personal, quickly went viral on social media. Sandlas is one of Punjabi music's most recognisable female voices, with a large following across India and the diaspora. The public announcement adds a joyful personal milestone to what has been a strong period professionally for the artist.
stories.lens: Jasmine Sandlas choosing a live concert stage — rather than a social-media post — to announce her engagement reflects a refreshing candour from a pop artist whose fans feel a genuine personal connection with her.
stories.article:
Punjabi pop singer Jasmine Sandlas turned her Delhi concert into a surprise engagement announcement, introducing her fiancé to the audience with the words "This is my man" — a moment that was captured on multiple phones in the crowd and quickly spread across Instagram and X.

Sandlas, who rose to national prominence with Dhurandhar, has cultivated a reputation for authenticity and directness, both in her music and in her public persona. The decision to make such a personal announcement live on stage, rather than through a carefully crafted social-media reveal, felt entirely in keeping with that image — and the crowd's reaction was rapturous.

The singer has been a consistent presence in Punjabi music for years, collaborating with some of the industry's biggest names and building a substantial following not just in Punjab but among Indian diaspora communities worldwide. Her love life has attracted curiosity from fans, making the on-stage reveal all the more impactful.

The clip has since been widely shared, with fans and fellow artists sending congratulations. For Sandlas, the moment marks a happy personal chapter — and for the Delhi audience that witnessed it live, an unexpectedly memorable concert night.
key_facts: Jasmine Sandlas introduced her fiancé on stage at a Delhi concert
Said 'This is my man' to the audience
Sandlas is known for the song Dhurandhar
